newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
55 PCT TURNOUT IN UTTAR PRADESH POLL AMIDST VIOLENCE

The second phase of assembly polls for 160 constituencies in Uttar Pradesh recorded 50 to 55 percent voter turnout amidst violence and killings. Polling was peaceful in Badaun district from where Defence Minister and Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav and former Chief Minister Mayawati were contesting. Muzaffarnagar district witnessed violent clashes leaving two persons shot dead and over 24 persons wounded.
Indian Express
FODDER SCAM PUTS UNITED FRONT IN A FIX

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officer probing the Bihar fodder scam probe declined to share his report with the CBI chief following a directive to this effect by Bihar High Court. This created tensions in the United Front government which immediately despatched the additional solicitor general to settle the matter with the chief justice of Bihar. Several politicians of the state, including the chief minister had allegedly pocketed millions costing the state losses to the tune of seven billion rupees. Janata Dal, the main constituent of United Front, is running government in Bihar.
The Economic Times
NEW FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT GUIDELINES SOON

The government is reportedly finalising policy guidelines on the composition of foreign direct investment (FDI) in sectors where a ceiling is in place. This is to allow greater clarity and transparency in FDI approvals. Major areas with FDI caps for Joint Ventures (JV) include telecommunication, civil aviation and banking. Plans are on board to allow foreign companies to channel indirect equity into their JV over and above the FDI ceiling of investments companies, provided they have majority Indian stake and management is in Indian hands.
STATE BANK'S GDR ISSUE OVERSUBSCRIBED

Despite sustained hammering of State Bank of India (SBI) scrips by foreign institutional investors, SBI's global depositary receipt (GDR) was eventualy priced well. SBI and its global coordinators announced the pricing of SBI's offering at $14.15 per GDR. This amounted to a 5.12 percent premium over SBI's underlying shares. The GDR issue was oversubscribed by over two times and the issue size was finalised at $369.98 million.
INTERIM POWER POLICY BY DECEMBER

The government may announce an interim policy for the power sector in December. The interim policy is expected to improve upon the 1991 announcements by previous Congress government which opened private sector investment in the power sector but offered little transparency. The interim policy would pave the way to expedite the pending memorandums of understanding with domestic and overseas independent power producers.
Financial Express
16.24 BLN RUPEE WORTH FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROPOSALS CLEARED

The Industry Ministry has cleared foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals worth 16.24 billion rupees in shipping, drugs, chemicals, engineering and floriculture sectors. The largest FDI of 4.34 billion rupees was allowed in Haldia Petrochemicals to raise the cracker capacity of 0.42 million TPA from the present 0.3 TPA. Cargill Asia Pacific plans venturing into flour milling with a capital investment of $25 million in its Indian subsidiary, involving FDI of 875 million rupees.
RELIANCE COMPANIES FINED FOR DELAY IN TRANSFER OF SHARES

The Company Law Board slapped a penalty of one million rupees each on Reliance Industries (RIL) and Reliance Capital Services for a delay in transfer of RIL Shares. It also fined all six RIL directors 100,000 rupees each. The Bombay bourse did not react to the developments as the RIL scrip fell marginally to 189 rupees from the previous closing of 190.75 rupees.
MERRIL LYNCH HAILS INDIA'S REFORMS

Global investment bank Merrill Lynch hailed India's economic reforms as one of the most successful among emerging markets. It said country's outlook was positive under the United Front government. India's macro economic fundamentals were currently very positive, Merrill Lynch said in a global economics and currencies report. It said inflation was trending down, balance of payment position was sound, rupee was expected to ease, and the economy was becoming more open and better integrated with the global market.
COCA COLA TO INVEST $700 MLN MORE IN INDIA

Coca Cola plans to set up two more subsidiaries in India. The multinational's move is based on expectations of a three-fold increase in its volume over five years. For this Coca Cola would have to raise its investment by six times the present level. Coca Cola's $700 million investment proposals include South Asia Holdings's plans to set up two subsidiaries in which all the bottling companies would be merged.
OVER 100 FOREIGN INVESTORS AWAITING GOVERNMENT CLEARANCE

India could be fast losing its emerging market status among foreign institutional investors (FIIs). It is understood that the once buoyant FIIs interest in India was declining due to poor performance of Indian stocks in domestic and overseas markets. Presently, some 100 new FIIs are awaiting government clearance. The bourse regulator and the central bank are reportedly in the process of clearing applications of these FIIs. Once the proposals are cleared, the total number of FIIs registered with Indian authorities would go up to over 550.
STATE BANK SCRIPS NOSEDIVE ON BEAR PRESSURE

The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) sensitive index dipped below the 3,200 mark to touch a new low of 3,190.36. State Bank of India (SBI)'s scrips fell by ten points due to bear hammering by foreign investors. SBI scrips crashed by 10.75 rupees to 239 rupees. The BSE index dipped by 31.03 points to 3,195.77. The National index was down by 7.57 points at 1,439.86.
Business Standard
EXPORT GROWTH DIPS TO 9.8 PCT

India's export growth rate during April-August declined sharply to 9.8 percent compared with same period last year. Exports touched a cumulative figure of $14.9 billion as compared with 37 percent in the same period last year. The non-oil imports during the period declined by 3.2 percent. Worried by the fall, the Commerce Ministry was studying reasons for the dismal trade performance and required policy responses to reverse the trend.
PLANNING COMMISSION WANTS CEILING ON GOVT BORROWING

The Planning Commission is reportedly framing broad parameters on government borrowings, divestment in the public sector and foreign investments for the Ninth Plan period (1997-2002). 46 percent of the government's revenue receipts now goes towards interest payments. The commission wanted the government to reduce its reliance on borrowings. The Commission said a limit should be fixed on government borrowings in relation to the gross domestic product and annual revenue.
INFLATION-LINKED BONDS PROPOSAL SHOT DOWN

The proposal of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to issue inflation-indexed bonds was shot down by the Finance Minister. RBI had sent the proposal to the Finance Ministry as part of its efforts to protect the savings of fixed-income groups in a high inflation rate regime. However, the minister felt that time was not ripe for issuing such new generation debt instruments.
FREE CAPITAL FLOW FRAUGHT WITH RISK: FINANCE MINISTER

Complete freedom in respect of capital transactions could be harmful to the developing countries, said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. The was so because the developing countries had limited ability to deal with volatility of capital flows and capital flights could occur in crisis situations, he said. Chidambaram made this point while addressing the joint annual discussion of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington. Chidambaram also argued for increase in the flow of World Bank's lending to India to support the infrastructure sector.
The Observer
GOVT PRUNES LIST FOR AUTOMATIC FDI APPROVAL

Faced with opposition from Left parties, the Industry Ministry has decided to prune the list of industries for automatic approval of foreign direct investment. The ministry had earlier recommended about 25 new industries to be included in the list for automatic approval. They included transport, mining, consultancy and financial services. The ministry has also decided against raising the limit for automatic approval of foreign investment from the existing 51 percent to 74 percent in some industries.
Business Line
BOURSE REGULATOR ISSUES NORMS FOR CUSTODIANS

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the bourse regulator, has asked all custodians to become members of the clearing houses of bourses by October-end. SEBI also directed them to participate in the clearing and settlement process through the clearing house/corporation for all securities. The bourse regulator called upon all the custodians in country to follow uniform norms in their dealings with clients, brokers, stock exchanges and depositories.
